episode_title: #90 Lynnard Cucksey: Advanced Materials and Battery Council

real_qa.q: What is the Advanced Materials and Battery Council and what role does it play in Australia's battery industry?
real_qa.r: The Advanced Materials and Battery Council was founded in 2022 by the research sector and industry and now has almost 50 members. It is a peak body covering the end-to-end value chain for batteries and advanced materials, with members ranging from Rio Tinto at resource extraction to deployment companies. It provides representation across Australia's battery ecosystem from minerals through to battery technology and advanced materials.
real_qa.requete: Advanced Materials Battery Council Australia what is

real_qa.q: How much funding is committed to Australia's Cheaper Home Battery Program and what are its implications?
real_qa.r: There is $7.2 billion committed over four years for the Cheaper Home Battery Program, which is $1 billion more than the $6.2 billion 13-year industrial development plan put in place for automotive. However, this program has no local content requirement, meaning the opportunity to spend money in a way that creates local jobs and investment outcomes for manufacturing capability has been missed.
real_qa.requete: Cheaper Home Battery Program 7.2 billion Australia funding

real_qa.q: What specific capital insurance mechanism has the United States implemented to support industrial battery and critical minerals manufacturing?
real_qa.r: The US has allocated $4 billion in insurance to back approximately $400 billion of debt for industrial manufacturing and processing projects. This mechanism allows banks to write loans to manufacturers and processors and sell off the risk to the market at the portfolio level, making it profitable and enabling the machinery of capital to flow into productive industry.
real_qa.requete: US 4 billion debt insurance industrial manufacturing battery

real_qa.q: What role does Alpha HPA play in Queensland's battery and advanced materials ecosystem?
real_qa.r: Alpha HPA, located in Gladstone, operates the world's largest single-site high-purity aluminum plant producing 10,000 tons per year. It supplies both the battery industry and high-growth sectors like semiconductors and AI data centers, serving as an example of how backing the middle of the value chain adds significant value to Australia's resources and creates demand signals for investability.
real_qa.requete: Alpha HPA Gladstone aluminum plant Queensland battery

real_qa.q: How many home batteries have been installed in Australia in the last 18 months?
real_qa.r: 440,000 home batteries have been installed in Australia in the last 18 or so months, representing a significant portion of Australia's battery deployment alongside large-scale grid batteries and vehicle batteries.
real_qa.requete: Australia home batteries installed 440000 last 18 months

real_qa.q: Why does Holden's historical manufacturing approach demonstrate unique Australian competitive advantages in advanced materials?
real_qa.r: Holden developed vehicle platforms for approximately one-sixth of the cost of equivalent vehicles from allied national manufacturers, demonstrating that Australia developed uniquely world-class capability while doing a lot with very little. This forced efficiency created genuine top-level capability without the capital resources of Europe or the US, resulting in unique Australian skills in competitive manufacturing.
real_qa.requete: Holden cost manufacturing advantage Australia one-sixth

guest.bio_context: Lynnard began his career as an engineer at Holden during the global financial crisis, where he gained experience in automotive manufacturing. He later transitioned into industrial policy, joining South Australia's Premier's Automotive Transformation Task Force, and subsequently worked in federal government roles including ownership of the Automotive Transformation Scheme ($600 billion policy from 2008). He spent years consulting to governments and corporations on lower-footprint transport solutions, worked with Rove on electric ute development, and served as battery lead for the Commonwealth Government's Powering Australia Growth Centre before leading the Advanced Materials and Battery Council.
